      PUBLIC INPUT
        1. Two 15-minute Public Input sessions will be allowed during each Council
           Meeting. Time will be divided equally among those wishing to speak, however,
           no person will be allowed to speak for more than 5 minutes.
        2. No person may address the council more than twice on any issue in any
           meeting. Comments must be addressed to the Chair and must not be personal
           or derogatory about any other person.
        3. Any questions must be directly related to the topic being discussed and must
           be addressed to the Chair only, who after consultation with Council and Town
           Administrator, will determine if the question can be answered at that time.
           Questions cannot be directed to an individual Councilor and must not be
           personal in nature. Issues raised during Public Input, which cannot be resolved
           or answered at that time, or which require additional discussion or research,
           will be noted by the Town Administrator who will be responsible for researching
           and responding to the comment directly during normal work hours or by
           bringing to the Council for discussion at a subsequent meeting. The Chair
           reserves the right to end questioning if the questions depart from clarification to
           deliberation.
        4. Council members may request a comment be added to New Business at a
           subsequent meeting.
                   Anyone requesting auxiliary aids or services is asked to contact
                the Administration Department five business days prior to the meeting.

STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         $2,000 check(s) ($1,500 Town & $500 Library) from HealthTrust to the Town of
               Hooksett for the 2025 town-wide wellness program(s) per RSA 31:95-b, III (b).
Meeting:       Town Council - 09 Apr 2025
Department:    Administration
Staff Contact: Donna Fitzpatrick, Human Resource Coordinator

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
HealthTrust provides healthcare coverage to New Hampshire public sector employees. The Town of Hooksett contracts with
HealthTrust for the Town's medical (Anthem) and dental (Delta) coverage. As a HealthTrust member, they offer our Town a Wellness
Coordinator Program. Four (4) Town employees have completed the academy as Wellness Coordinators for CY2025 (Donna
Fitzpatrick, HR Coordinator, Francine Swafford, Police Executive Asst., Evelyn Horn, PW Executive Asst., and Chris Larochelle,
Patron Services Librarian). These coordinators help to motivate our co-workers to make healthy choices, to incorporate a culture of
health in their work environments and promote healthy programs.

HealthTrust has provided our Town $2,000 check(s) ($1,500 Town & $500 Library) toward the implementation of our CY2025 town-
wide wellness program(s), based on Hooksett's completed 2024 Wellness Campaigns (see below):

Campaign Name (Dates)
    “Try Something New” Well Being for a Well Rounded You (04/18/2024 - 05/22/2024)
Campaign Goal
    Try new things and gain different perspectives by reframing your thoughts, reconnecting with your goals and taking a
deeper look into what inspires you.
Campaign Description
    Well-Being includes mental, physical, emotional, environmental, spiritual and financial wellness. This year, try new
things and gain different perspectives by reframing your thoughts, reconnecting with your goals and taking a deeper look
into what inspires you. By working on being a well-rounded individual, you will be able to help those around you become
their best selves, too! (Town will send pamphlet distributed to all employees (active & retired) to our Wellness Advisor.
Campaign Budget Total $2,694.56 spent
Campaign Details
        01/22/2024 Wellness Coordinator Brainstorming meeting for 2024 Wellness Program
        01/22/2024-03/07/20241) create program poster, general notice, pamphlets & bingo cards, 2) order trivia cards,
         inspirational stones, multi-color waterproof sport pouches, birdhouses (for “It Takes a Village Contest”)
        03/07/2024 Post program general notice in all departments (to spark interest something is coming)
         03/11/2024 print & fold program pamphlets
        04/04/2024 payroll stuffer – 2024 Wellness Kick-off Notice (will forward pics/handouts to wellness advisor)
        04/10/2024 wellness coordinators assemble wellness items to distribute on 4/18/24 to each employee
        04/18/2024 wellness program kick-off at annual employee appreciation luncheon. 1) HealthTrust = wellness
         presentation to employees by Katrina Manning (SMP, etc.), 2) BassPro = Nerf archery “Try Something New”-
         those who participated received logo hat, 3) Planet Fitness – educational material and raffle for 1 yr free
         membership (will forward handout to wellness advisor).
        04/18/2024 Distributed “Try Something New” goodies into a reusable box to each employee: *pamphlet detailing
         wellness program, *bingo card, *multi-color waterproof sport pouch, water bottle, Veggies Stixs, and wooden bird
         houses (It Takes a Village contest) (*retiree mailing contents). (will forward handouts to wellness advisor)

STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         Town Council Vacancy to replace the seat vacated by Vincent Lembo Jr effective
               April 1, 2025
Meeting:       Town Council - 09 Apr 2025
Department:    Administration
Staff Contact: Geraldine Ciardelli, Executive Assistant

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
At the March 12, 2025 Town Meeting, Vincent Lembo Jr announced he was officially stepping down
as a Town Council member effective April 1, 2025. His hope was that someone newly elected to the
Council at the March 11 vote would step in early and get an early start. Per the Charter Section 3.3,
:Vacancies occurring in the office the Councilor at any time shall be filled by a duly qualified member
by appointment by affirmative vote of the Council within thirty (30) days of a declared vacancy". The
position was advertised on the Town of Hooksett website on March 13, 2025 and in the Manchester
Union Leader on March 20, 2025. Received applications are being reviewed and will be discussed at
this meeting

RECOMMENDATION:
Review, discuss and select a Town Councilor

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Motion to appoint a new Town Councilor to complete term of vacated seat in accordance with Section
3.3 (Vacancies) of the Town Charter.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
I agree with the suggested motion.

ATTACHMENTS:
Town Council - 09 Apr 2025 - Agenda

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:                Town Council
Title:             Consideration of Outdoor Dining Ordinance
Meeting:           Town Council - 09 Apr 2025
Department:        Community Development
Staff Contact:     Grant McGregor, Town Planner

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
There have been significant changes to the Outdoor Dining ordinance since its introduction in 2024.
The previous proposal was based on Derry's ordinance. Change in Staff disconnected the work on
the Ordinance, resulting in Planning Board and Zoning Board Chairs requesting that the 2024 Public
Hearing be closed. The Public Hearing was closed at the October 23, 2024 Town Council Meeting. A
new Outdoor Dining ordinance was developed by the Development Regulations Subcommittee. The
ordinance is based on Franklin, NH and has fewer design requirements than Derry, NH. This
ordinance proposal underwent discussion on Mach 12 and a Public Hearing on March 26.

Based on the discussion during the Public Hearing, the Development Regulations Subcommittee
revised insurance to only be required with Town of Hooksett as additional insured on public property.
Previously, the Town of Hooksett was required to be listed as both the certificate holder and
additional insured on private property. The dollar amount was unchanged based on information that
received from the Subcommittee that the dollar amounts listed are near the minimum required for
restaurants.

The ordinance is now eligible for a vote if the Council determines that the changes made since the March 26
Public Hearing are not substantive.

FINANCIAL IMPACT:
Small revenue for the processing of the application fee of $100.

RECOMMENDATION:
Review the changes made to the ordinance since the Public Hearing and determine if the changes are
substantive. If the changes are not substantive, vote on the ordinance. If the changes are substantive, require an
additional public hearing.

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Move that the changes are substantial. If yes, an additional public hearing is required starting from
the beginning of the process under Town Council Rules of Procedure Section 13(a). If no, move to
vote on the Outdoor Dining Ordinance.

ATTACHMENTS:

                       TOWN OF HOOKSETT
                  Outdoor Dining Policy & Regulations
                           (Adopted _____)

Purpose & Applicability

The Town of Hooksett recognizes the importance of outdoor dining to the vitality
and success of its eating establishments. The purpose of this ordinance is to
accommodate the growing demand for outdoor dining while promoting the
health, safety and welfare of our residents and visitors while dining outdoors.
Existing restaurants without approved outdoor dining service at the time of
adoption of this ordinance, upon application for outdoor dining service, may be
reviewed under this ordinance.

Definitions

Outdoor Dining Service:
Provision of wait staff, and food service outdoors.
Long-term Application:
An application for seasonal (public property) or year-round (private property) outdoor
dining service. A long-term application expires upon change of ownership, alteration of
outdoor dining layout, or change of use.
Public Land/Property:
Property owned by the Town of Hooksett or the State of New Hampshire.
Private Land/Property:
Property owned by any party other than Town of Hooksett or the State of New
Hampshire.

Application Procedure

1. The application fee is $100.00.

2. Community Development and Fire Department review the application to ensure
   compliance with Town of Hooksett Development Regulations, Town of Hooksett
   Zoning Ordinance, New Hampshire Fire Code as defined in RSA 153:1, VI-a., and
   New Hampshire Building Code as defined in RSA 155-A:1, IV.

3. Three (3) copies of the application form shall be submitted to the Community
   Development office. One (1) electronic (PDF) copy shall be sent to the Community
   Development office.

4. Three (3) 11” x 17” site plans, two (2) 22” x 36” site plans, and one (1) electronic
(PDF) site plan depicting the area to be used for outdoor dining shall be submitted to the
Community Development office. Application Requirements, as set forth below and
referenced on page two (2) of the application form, shall be submitted with each


                                                                                             Page 16 of 72
                                                                                    Agenda Item #16.1.


application.

Application Requirements

1. A long-term application includes Assembly Permit approvals from the Code
   Enforcement
Officer and Fire Department.

2. An 8 ½” x 11” plan detailing:
     a. Lot lines and the orientation of the building on the lot
     b. Dimensions of building and the lot
     c. Street location, width, and curbing location
     d. Access points and traffic circulation
     e. Setback dimensions from sidewalk to building
     f. Location of proposed outdoor dining area and its components
              i. Total square feet of the dining area
              ii. The number and location of tables and chairs, noting the
              separation distance between the tables and aisle widths
              iii. Location of equipment and accessories.
              iv. Location of pedestrian access points and sidewalk separation
              v. Location of any ramps, fire hydrants, fire lanes, light poles,
              natural features, parking spaces, and trash receptacles
              vi. Location of any proposed outdoor bar
              vii. Location and dimension of barriers
              viii. Drawings or photos of proposed barriers, umbrellas, tables,
              chairs

3. On public property, certificate of Insurance $1,000,000 per
occurrence/$2,000,000 aggregate. - The Town of Hooksett must be listed as
additional insured. The certificate must be valid throughout the period of the
permit.

         a) For long-term applications: Annual verification of insurance coverage
            is required and may be submitted by PDF to the Community
            Development office. If insurance lapses, outdoor dining permit is
            expired.

4. Commitment to indemnify the Town.

5. A copy of the Applicant’s license from New Hampshire Liquor
Commission, if applicant intends to serve alcohol. New Hampshire Liquor
Commission license requires extension of service approval.

Standard Conditions

1. Long-term applications shall be in effect from April 1 through


                                                                                         Page 17 of 72
                                                                                        Agenda Item #16.1.


     November 1 on public property and year-round on private property.

2.   For the period from November 2 through the following March 31, all chairs,
     fencing, umbrellas, tables and other equipment must be removed from public
     property. Furniture that is not removed by applicable deadlines may be subject
     to removal and disposal at the business owner’s cost.

3. It is the Applicant’s responsibility to ensure that all movable items within
public property are secured against wind or theft. The Town accepts no liability for
lost, stolen or damaged property.

4. For the period from April 1 through the following November 1, all chairs, fencing,
umbrellas, tables, and other equipment shall be removed from public property upon 24-
hour notice from the Code Enforcement Officer.

5. Outdoor dining is permitted from 8:00 a.m. until 10:00 p.m.

6. The long-term application is not transferable.

7. An outdoor dining permit does not increase the maximum number of patrons
allowed inside the eating establishment. The outdoor permit is only for the
additional outside seats. Place of Assembly numbers for the indoor portion of a
restaurant shall not be increased by the addition of outdoor dining.

8. Outdoor dining areas shall be setback five (5) feet from a crosswalk, handicap ramp,
driveway or intersection.

9. A five (5) foot path for pedestrians is required on all impervious area outside
the outdoor dining area at all times.

     A. The 5- foot path must be a clear aisle that does not include any obstructions
        such as light poles, fire hydrants, sign posts, bollards, etc.

     B. The five (5) foot path shall not be within any vehicular travel lane.

10. All building entrances shall remain unobstructed and shall comply with the New
Hampshire Fire Code as defined by RSA 153:1, VI-a.

11. All outdoor dining areas shall be laid out in such a way that they maintain
compliance with the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and
maintain compliance with RSA 354-A:16 and RSA 354-A:17.

12. Outdoor dining areas must be contiguous to the licensed premises, unless otherwise
specified in Standard Condition 13.
13. Outdoor dining areas may be separated from the licensed premises, provided the


                                                                                             Page 18 of 72
                                                                                    Agenda Item #16.1.


outdoor dining area is enclosed using materials as approved by the Code Enforcement
Officer.

14. Businesses must use their own trash and recycle receptacles. Outdoor
    dining area must be cleared of all debris after close of business each
    day.
15. Outdoor dining shall not damage sidewalks, curbing, bike racks, street trees,
light poles, trash containers or other Town infrastructure. The use of hardware
which punctures publicly owned pavement, poles, or siding is prohibited. It is
recommended that metal chairs, tables, and umbrellas are equipped with rubber
padding to prevent any damage. The Town also encourages the use of wooden
tables to reduce the possibly of any damage.

16. All impervious areas outside the establishment must be completely free of snow and
     ice.

17. Umbrellas are permitted within a vertical line directly above the outdoor dining
area. Umbrellas must be kept in good condition, of consistent design and high-quality
materials. Umbrellas cannot be torn, tattered, or faded in any manner.

18. Tents/canopies over the outdoor dining area are not permitted. Such coverings
require site plan review by the Planning Board.

19. Heaters require specific approval from the Fire Chief.

20. Decorations must be fire retardant and meet New Hampshire Fire Code Standards.
Any loose hanging material is prohibited.

21. Fire alarm pull stations must not be obstructed.

22. Open flames (i.e. – candles, torches, etc.) are prohibited.

23. Sufficient lighting is required. Extension cords are not permitted without prior
written consent from the Code Enforcement Officer.

24. No smoking within outdoor dining areas on public property.


                                                                                         Page 19 of 72
                                                                                      Agenda Item #16.1.


Environmental Health Conditions

1. The outdoor dining and exterior area are to be left in a clean and sanitary
condition at all times and garbage contained at all times in covered receptacles.

2. The outdoor dining area shall be left in clean condition at the close of
business with all garbage and their containers removed from the area and any
ground debris swept up at the close of business daily. Nothing in this section
shall be interpreted to lessen the requirements found in RSA 143 or other state
statute, code or rule.

3. The area shall be kept free from rodent harborage and infestation. Where
rodents are found, they shall be promptly exterminated by approved processes
that will not be injurious to human health. After pest elimination, proper
precautions shall be taken to eliminate rodent harborage and prevent
reinfestation. Enforcement of this subsection shall be by the Code Enforcement
Officer.

4. No food preparation, grilling, service windows, service counters or wait
stations shall be allowed in the area and no condiments, paper products or the like
shall be stored in the outdoor area.

5. The Fire Department will review that interior bathroom facilities are
sufficient to support the additional outdoor seating. Exterior restrooms are
prohibited.

6. All outdoor dining activities must comply with the New Hampshire Fire
Code as defined by RSA 153:1, VI-a, as amended.

Compliance

All outdoor dining permits are subject to revocation by the Town for failure to
comply with the conditions of the permit, ordinance, or any rules and regulations
established by the Town or its Departments. Permit holders who damage public
property may be held responsible for the replacement, cleaning or repair of
impacted public property.

Town Authority

The Town may terminate or alter use or configuration of outdoor dining areas on
public spaces in order to facilitate public or private construction projects, road
closures associated with special events or festivals, or any other public purpose.
The Town may suspend, terminate or modify this outdoor dining program at any
time in accordance with the procedure for removal of “Other Ordinances.”

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:               Town Council
Title:            Cardiac Monitor / Defibrillator Purchase for Ambulance Service
Meeting:          Town Council - 09 Apr 2025
Department:       Fire and Rescue
Staff Contact:    Joseph Stalker, Captain

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The Fire Rescue Department's ambulance service operates three (3) ambulances and responds to
over 2,600 emergency calls each year. On our ambulances, one of the most commonly utilized
pieces of equipment is the cardiac monitor / defibrillator. This device is utilized on every single call; to
obtain vital signs on a sick patient all the way up to delivering life-saving defibrillations to patients in
cardiac arrest. Of our three (3) current cardiac monitor / defibrillators, two (2) have exceeded their
recommended life-span and the third monitor is approaching it. As this is a large expenditure, we
have spent considerable time exploring different options in order to determine the best device for our
service delivery while finding the most cost-effective method to replace these devices. In February,
Stryker, the manufacturer of our current cardiac monitor / defibrillators presented a 0% financing
option that allowed us to save a significant amount of money as opposed to other options. We
believe this is a valuable and cost-effective opportunity to replace the devices and will allow us to
continue providing a high level of quality medical care to our community. This quote / purchase also
includes crash-rated mounts for the ambulances, all the needed accessories to operate and upgraded
modems allowing providers to communicate with the hospitals and provide early notification for life-
saving treatments. Additionally, this purchase includes a one (1) year warranty on the equipment and
a 4-year service plan, essentially covering the devices for the length of the financing. Having these
devices serviced and calibrated on a regular basis keeps these devices operating properly, while
providing liability coverage for our department. Our current service / maintenance contract costs
$5,651.65 annually to maintain the three (3) cardiac monitor / defibrillators we have now. Whereas
the service plan is pre-purchased with these devices, this provides an additional savings of
$28,258.25 over the course of the financing plan, reducing the annual net cost of these devices to
$29,221.81 ($34,873.46 - $5,651.65).

FINANCIAL IMPACT:
A total cost of $174,367.30 financed over the course of 5 years at 0% interest; five (5) annual
payments of $34,873.46 paid out of the Ambulance Revenue Account to Stryker. An annual savings
of $5,561.65 will occur due to cancellation of our current cardiac monitor service plans.

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
Town purchasing policy will be followed for this purchase, including the use of Sourcewell pricing.

RECOMMENDATION:


                                                                                                      Page 24 of 72
                                                                                          Agenda Item #17.1.


Recommend the purchase of three (3) Stryker LifePak35 cardiac monitor / defibrillators through the
0%, 5-year financing option provided by Stryker for a total amount of $174,367.30, to be paid from the
Ambulance Revenue Account.

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Motion to allow the Town Administrator to enter into a contract for the purchase of three (3) Stryker
LifePak35 cardiac monitor/defibrillators through the 0%, 5-year financing option provided by Stryker
for a total amount of $174,367.30, paid for out of the Ambulance Revenue Account.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
I agree with the suggested motion.

                           ADDITIONAL SERVICE NARRATIVE 02
                       Phase 3 – Limited Construction Phase Services

                                       March 13, 2025

The original contract, dated May 31, 2023, and executed on June 8, 2023, between the Town of
Hooksett, New Hampshire (Hooksett) and Gale Associates, Inc. (Gale) is to be modified as
follows for limited construction phase services.

Per Hooksett’s request, Gale provided Hooksett with two (2) Design Documents including one
(1) set of technical specifications and drawings for masonry repairs and throughwall flashing
installation, dated March 6, 2024, and one (1) set of technical specifications and drawings for
roof replacement at Roof Areas A, B, C, and D, dated August 1, 2024. As summarized in Item
MM1.7 of the 90% Roof Replacement Design Development Submission Review Meeting
Minutes, dated June 18, 2024, the intent was for Hooksett to bid and perform the masonry
repair scope of work prior to roof replacement. However, as Hooksett received only one (1)
proposal for the masonry repair scope of work, Hooksett has rebid the masonry documents
with the roof replacement scope of work to General Contractors.

It is Gale’s understanding that Hooksett has received proposals from General Contractors for
the masonry repair and roof replacement scope of work and has awarded the project to
Aberthaw Construction Company, Inc. (ACC) for an anticipated spring/summer construction.
Due to potential budgetary constraints, Hooksett has reported that they anticipate holding
construction meetings and coordinating with ACC during the course of construction. Hooksett
also anticipates self-performing the review of submittals provided by ACC, however, it is
Gale’s understanding that Hooksett may provide Gale with select product submittals for
review and approval. Hooksett has requested that Gale assist by providing limited
construction phase services including review of select product submittals provided to Gale by
Hooksett, performing site visits to review ongoing construction and mockups, and one (1)
punch list evaluation.

SCOPE OF SERVICES
Phase 1 – Evaluation and Design Services (completed under the original contract)

Phase 2 – Structural Augmentation Design – Roof Areas B, C, and D (completed under CA
01)

Phase 3 – Limited Construction Phase Services

Based upon our understanding of the project, we propose the following Scope of Service:

•   Initiate the construction phase by establishing the project site visit schedule during
    construction and points of contact for communication with Hooksett and ACC.

•   Receive and review contractor’s shop drawings and submittals for acceptance or
    rejection. This proposal is predicated on Hooksett receiving and distributing select
    Contractor’s submittals that they want Gale to review. Without authorization from
    Hooksett, Gale will not perform a review of submittals and shop drawings distributed to
    Gale by the Contractor. Submittals provided to Gale by Hooksett for review will be
    returned to Hooksett for distribution to ACC.

    o   This proposal is limited to sixteen (16) hours for a Staff Designer, four (4) hours for a
        Project Engineer, and four (4) hours for a Project Designer for this task. Office support
        in the form of the Project Manager’s review/comment of submittal reviews and
        administrative assistance to finalize and distribute the reviews are also included in
        these services.

•   Perform periodic observations of the contractor’s work at increments or dates requested
    by Hooksett. Written field reports outlining methods and materials of construction and
    progress will be submitted.

    o   This proposal is limited to:

            Six (6) half-day site visits for review of masonry repairs and roof replacement

             •   Half-day site visits include three (3) hours on site, travel to/from the site, and

                 are also included in these services.

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         Update the Town Council Rules of Procedure - Section #7a. and b. to reduce the
               number of Public Input sessions from two to one
Meeting:       Town Council - 09 Apr 2025
Department:    Administration
Staff Contact: Geraldine Ciardelli, Executive Assistant

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
We have two Public Input Sessions on our Town Council agenda. We would like to eliminate the
second Public Input session on the Town Council Agenda. We contacted like municipalities and found
the majority only have one Public Input session. And at a time when people are managing multiple
tasks, reducing to one session will help move the meetings along more efficiently.
Update the Rules of Procedure Section "7. Order of Business"

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
Change to the Rules of Procedure

RECOMMENDATION:
To remove the second Public Input Session from the Town Council agendas.

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Motion to approve Updated Rules of Procedure Section #7a. and b. (removal of the second Public
Input Session from the Town Council agendas) for an effective date of April 23, 2025

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
I agree with the suggested motion.

ATTACHMENTS:
ROP - reduce to 1 public input

      Town of Hooksett
Town Council Rules of Procedures

   Adopted as of: 01/10/2001
   Amended as of: 7/10/2024


                                    Page 71 of 72
                                                                                  Agenda Item #17.4.


1. ORDER OF BUSINESS
   The Town Council shall follow the below agenda order whenever possible for ease of
   transcription, audience participation and possible time restraints. The Council Chair,
   during the Agenda Overview, will inform the audience of any change in the agenda
   order for a particular meeting.

       a. Agenda Order of Council Meetings
              I. Call to Order
             II. Proof of Posting
            III. Roll Call
            IV. Pledge of Allegiance
             V. Agenda Overview
            VI. Public Hearings
           VII. Special Recognitions
           VIII. Public Input
            IX. Scheduled Appointments
             X. Consent Agenda
            XI. Nominations/Appointments
           XII. Brief Recess
           XIII. Old Business
          XIV. New Business
           XV. Approval of Minutes
          XVI. Town Administrator’s Report
          XVII. Town Council Future Items
         XVIII. Informational Items and Correspondence
          XIX. Subcommittee Reports
           XX. Public Input
          XXI. Non-Public Session NH RSA 91-A:3 II
          XXII. Adjournment
